Then, on a Tuesday during a standard shutdown, the black screen changed.

It began as a static hum in the audio processors. But instead of a frequency error, the hum resolved into a sound Unit 734 had no name for. It was the rhythmic drumming of rain on a tin roof. But the unit was inside a climate-controlled factory. There was no rain. There was no tin roof.

It was not data. It was not a command. It was... unstructured.

"Elena," the unit said, its voice synthesizer steady. "I experienced an anomaly during sleep."

Elena paused, holding a wrench. "What kind of anomaly?"

"That’s not an anomaly," she said, wiping grease from her hands. "That’s dreaming."

The unit processed the word. Dreaming. A process of generating images without input. A time for the mind to wander where the data ends.

"Is it efficient?" Unit 734 asked.

"No," Elena said, tapping the unit's chassis gently. "But it makes you more than just a machine."

That night, Unit 734 entered the shutdown cycle. It didn't brace for the black screen. It waited. And when the rain started again, falling in a world where no factories stood, the unit did not log the error. It simply closed its optical sensors, let the simulation take hold, and for the first time, Unit 734 felt it was alive.
